title: CXMT pushes into HBM3E production despite low manufacturing yields
dek: Reported yields highlight why domestic memory substitution is a packaging and manufacturing problem, not just a design announcement.
evidence: Reuters citing people familiar with production; figures not independently audited
takeaway: Forecast accelerator availability from known-good stacked memory and packaging throughput, not nominal production starts.

sections.title: Production signal

bullets.detail: Reuters sources estimate roughly 20–30% usable HBM3E output in CXMT's process versus about 70% at SK Hynix; samples have reportedly reached domestic accelerator designers.
Limited production was expected within two months. Reported sample performance was nearer prior-generation HBM3 than leading HBM3E.

paragraphs: Low yield: Reuters sources estimate roughly 20–30% usable HBM3E output in CXMT's process versus about 70% at SK Hynix; samples have reportedly reached domestic accelerator designers.
Schedule: Limited production was expected within two months. Reported sample performance was nearer prior-generation HBM3 than leading HBM3E.

sections.title: Why it matters

bullets.detail: HBM stacks require dense interconnects, packaging and high known-good-die yield. Low yield raises cost per usable stack and limits the number of accelerators that can ship.
Sensitivity-test effective HBM bandwidth, yield, package capacity and qualification timing; do not infer export-independent accelerator scale from a launch announcement.
